paco-duques.name: Palace of the Dukes of Braganza
paco-duques.short: A 15th-century palace with 39 brick chimneys and tapestries, rebuilt from ruin in 1937–1959
paco-duques.long: Afonso, Count of Barcelos and future first Duke of Braganza, began the palace around 1420 after his marriage to Constança de Noronha. The dukes soon moved to Vila Viçosa; the palace was quarried for stone and in the 19th century turned into a barracks. In 1937–1959 the architect Rogério de Azevedo rebuilt it on the model of northern European palaces. Today it houses a museum of Flemish tapestries and the President’s official residence in the north.
paco-duques.history:
The palace was commissioned by Afonso, illegitimate son of King John I and 8th Count of Barcelos. Back from missions to the courts of France, Venice, Aragon and Castile, he married Constança de Noronha as his second wife and around 1420 began a residence in Guimarães in the Burgundian fashion. The almost square plan with four corner towers recalls the Palace of the Kings of Majorca in Perpignan; 39 brick chimneys rise above the steep roofs. In 1442 Afonso became the first Duke of Braganza. He died in 1461, and his widow lived in the palace until 1480.

His heirs preferred Vila Viçosa in the south, and the palace emptied. In 1483 King John II executed the third duke for treason and confiscated the estates; they were returned in 1496, but the dukes never came back to Guimarães. In 1611 the Poor Clares and in 1666 the Capuchins were allowed to take stone from the palace for their convents. In 1807, during the French invasions, it became a barracks; soldiers stayed until 1935 and demolished the courtyard galleries to make a parade ground.

In 1933 Alfredo Guimarães, director of the Alberto Sampaio Museum, showed the ruin to Salazar. In 1937 the architect Rogério de Azevedo began the reconstruction. He travelled to Brussels, Antwerp and the Loire for models and rebuilt not so much what had been as what might have been; the work is still called controversial. Building went on until 1959. On 25 June 1959 the palace became the President’s official residence in the north, and on 26 August it opened as a museum.

The first-floor museum holds Flemish and French tapestries, oriental carpets, furniture, Chinese porcelain, the painting “Paschal Lamb” attributed to Josefa de Óbidos and a portrait of Catherine of Braganza. The banqueting hall has a timber vault, and the chapel is lit by stained glass. The palace has been a National Monument since 1910. It received 366,514 visitors in 2022 and 376,331 in 2024, making it one of the most visited monuments in northern Portugal.
facts: Building began around 1420, after Count Afonso’s second marriage.
Thirty-nine brick chimneys in the Burgundian manner rise above the roofs.
The palace served as a barracks from 1807 to 1935.
Rogério de Azevedo’s reconstruction ran from 1937 to 1959.
Since 25 June 1959 it has been the President of Portugal’s residence in the north.
paco-duques.tip: The palace opens daily from 10:00 to 18:00, last entry 17:30. A ticket costs €5, €8 combined with the castle, or €13 with the Alberto Sampaio Museum. Restoration work is under way, so some rooms may be closed. The statue of Afonso Henriques stands by the ramp in front, and the castle is a three-minute walk through the park.
